conventions.convention: The ordered coframe is (dx⁰,dx¹,dx²,dx³), the metric is diag(-1,1,1,1), and the positive volume form is dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³. The star is characterized by α∧⋆β=〈α,β〉η volη.
Periods use finite real smooth singular cycles and the finite signed sum of simplex pullback integrals. Exactness requires a globally defined smooth primitive.

The unit sphere has outward orientation and area form ωp(v,w)=p·(v×w). The spherical parameter order is (θ,φ), giving Φθ×Φφ=sinθ Φ; seam identifications and pole rank failures occur only on the parameter boundary.

The local primitive formula assumes an open subset of R⁴ star-shaped about a specified a∈U and a smooth closed two-form. The global equivalence uses vanishing de Rham class; a nonzero period is a sufficient obstruction, with no converse period criterion asserted.
The displayed tetrahedron vertex order has determinant -16, so its outward face coefficients are (-1)^(j+1). Radial projection is used only away from the origin.
The circulation example uses the positively traversed loop γ(t)=(cos(2πt),sin(2πt)), 0≤t≤1, and globally defined real-valued scalar primitives.

load_bearing.statement: For 0≤k≤4, the Lorentzian Hodge star is the unique linear map satisfying α∧⋆ηβ=〈α,β〉η volη for the specified oriented metric diag(-1,1,1,1); equivalently ⋆ηeᴵ=εI s(I,Iᶜ)eᴵᶜ. Periods are finite smooth-singular-cycle integrals, and exact forms have global smooth primitives.

On open U⊆R⁴ star-shaped about a∈U, a smooth closed two-form has the smooth primitive Aμ(x)=∫₀¹ t(x-a)νFνμ(a+t(x-a))dt. On any smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, a smooth closed two-form has a global smooth one-form potential iff its de Rham class is zero. A nonzero period on a finite smooth singular two-cycle precludes exactness.
For the outward-oriented unit sphere and ωp(v,w)=p·(v×w), the specified spherical parametrization is an admissible regular patch and ∫S²ω=4π.
For the fixed orientation and signature, ⋆η²=(-1)^(k(4-k)+1) id for 0≤k≤4. In particular, ⋆η²=-id on two-forms, ⋆η(dx⁰∧dx¹)=-dx²∧dx³, and ⋆η(dx²∧dx³)=dx⁰∧dx¹.

concerns.concern: Verification step 4.1 reads “∫zβ=4π e0”. The suffix “e0” is malformed and does not express the intended nonzero comparison. Step 3.1 already proves the exact value 4π, so the nonexactness deduction is recoverable.

Fact F1 says def-emx-lorentz-star “fixes F=½Fμν dxμ∧dxν”, but that supplier's Definition does not state this component convention. The theorem's own Statement supplies the expression, so the calculation is supported locally; the attribution should identify that local convention.

seams_checked.note: Checked the excitation definition, exterior-Maxwell theorem, and vacuum-duality theorem against the supplier definitions and sign lemma. The (-+++) orientation, star²=-id, and vacuum closure signs agree. The C¹ chain-flux treatment uses its separate continuous-integral and C¹ Stokes suppliers rather than strengthening the smooth period theorem.

The topological-flux example applies the 4π outward sphere integral and nonzero-period obstruction to an explicitly constructed smooth cycle. The PEC example uses ⋆(dx²∧dx³)=dx⁰∧dx¹ and consequently Eθ=-cB₀e₁. Both preserve the supplier conventions and conditional physical scope.

The helicity-line-bundle definition imports the ordered spatial orientation from the fixed spacetime coframe. Its outward sphere orientation and right-handed cross product agree with the supplier; it does not infer bundle topology from the Lorentzian star-square result.
